author: A. K. Farrar
title: Monarchs end season with loss to Georgia State in Sun Belt tournament
text:
The Old Dominion University Monarchs baseball team ended its season on May 20 after a 17-1 loss to Georgia State in the first round of the Sun Belt Conference tournament at DABOS Park.
The defeat marks the conclusion of an up-and-down year for Old Dominion, which finished with a record of 29-26. The Monarchs faced challenges throughout the season, including extensive travel due to stadium renovations and limited opportunities to play at home.
Georgia State advances in the tournament and will next face Southern Miss. For Old Dominion, Head Coach Chris Finwood became the program’s all-time winningest coach this year. Despite that milestone, Finwood said after the game, “You certainly have to give credit where it’s due and Georgia State just kicked our butts tonight. They just played great tonight. We started out the season 5-10 and our guys fought so hard the second half of the season. Maybe we just ran out of gas a little bit.”
Georgia State pitcher Cole Roberts held ODU to one hit over six innings as his team built a commanding lead early in the game. The Panthers scored two runs before ODU had a chance to bat and continued adding runs throughout, eventually leading by fifteen runs before Old Dominion got on the scoreboard with a home run from senior Maverick Stallings in the seventh inning.
This season was marked by construction delays at ODU’s Ellmer Family Baseball Complex, forcing most games away from campus or played with temporary seating added by order of President Brian O. Hemphill, PhD., while permanent facilities remained unfinished. The new stadium is expected to be ready for use next February.
Finwood reflected on his team’s perseverance through these challenges: “You hate to finish here on this note,” he said. “Having said that, I’m really proud of this group…I thought our guys showed a lot of character and resilience.” He also praised Stallings: “Maverick wasn’t named to any of the all-conference teams, but he had an all-conference year…He walked onto his junior college and ended up having a great career at ODU.”
Looking ahead, Finwood expressed optimism about playing in their renovated facility next season: “Once the stadium is done, it’s really going to be a shot in the arm for our program. That’s something we’re all looking forward to.”
